key: Revile not those unto whom they pray beside Allah lest they wrongfully revile Allah through ignorance.
s: After the Prophet is told he is no keeper over the idolaters, the believers are addressed; Ibn Kathir, on 6:108, reads it as a benefit given up for fear of a greater harm, since reviling the idolaters’ gods brings God reviled in return.

evidence.words: وَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَنْ سَبِّ آلِهَةِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ مَصْلَحَةٌ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ يَتَرَتَّبُ عَلَيْهِ مَفْسَدَةٌ أَعْظَمُ مِنْهَا، وَهِيَ مُقَابَلَةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ بِسَبِّ إِلَهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَهُوَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ.
evidence.gloss: [God forbids His Messenger] and the believers to revile the gods of the idolaters: even if there be some benefit in it, a greater harm follows from it, namely the idolaters answering by reviling the God of the believers, who is God, there is no god but He.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-An’am 6:108, at 896). Plain sense faithful: 6:107 tells the Prophet he is not set as a keeper over the idolaters, and 6:108 turns to a plural address; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 6:108 Ibn Kathir opens by saying God forbids the Messenger and the believers to revile the idolaters’ gods, since even if there is benefit in it a greater harm follows, the idolaters reviling God in return; later in the same comment he names this as giving up a benefit for a harm that outweighs it (ترك المصلحة لمفسدة أرجح منها), citing the hadith on reviling one’s parents. The sentence paraphrases exactly this. Evidence is a contiguous span of the opening sentence (the proposer’s basis had ellipses and began at a honorific sign). 42 words; entry-check ok.
